principle_violations.reason: The DebitPaymentProcessor class directly depends on the concrete implementation of SMSAuthorizer. This means the payment processor shouldn’t be concerned with how its payment is validated, whether that be by SMS, a robot check, or an email. This violates the Dependency Inversion Principle since the high-level class DebitPaymentProcessor is directly dependent on a low-level class.
principle_violations.suggestion: Instead of depending on concrete implementations, the high-level class DebitPaymentProcessor should depend on abstractions. Create an abstract class Authorizer. Now you can create SMSAuthorizer and NotARobotAuthorizer, which implement the Authorizer class.

principle_violations.reason: This code violates the Single Responsibility Principle because the order class is responsible for both prices and quantities.
principle_violations.suggestion: Split the Order class into two separate classes: one for the order quantities and one for the prices.
